payload.explanation:
Let $0=t_0<\cdots<t_n$ be the given finite partition and let $r_i$ be the continuous profiles. We prove
$$r_i(t)\ge -\frac{6}{1+4t}\qquad(t_i\le t\le t_{i+1})$$
under the lower right Dini inequality, the initial lower bound, and the upward-jump inequalities in the statement.

First consider one interval $[a,b]$ with $a\ge0$ and a continuous profile $r$ whose initial value is at least $-6/(1+4a)$. For $\varepsilon>0$, use the lower comparison function
$$b_\varepsilon(t)=-\frac{6}{1+4t}-\varepsilon.$$
The denominator is positive. Writing $A=6/(1+4t)>0$, its derivative satisfies
$$\frac23 b_\varepsilon(t)^2-b_\varepsilon'(t)
=\frac43 A\varepsilon+\frac23\varepsilon^2>0.$$
Thus, at a contact point, the assumed lower right Dini derivative of $r$ is strictly larger than the derivative of $b_\varepsilon$. The one-dimensional comparison principle, applied to the negative profile, gives $r\ge b_\varepsilon$ on the closed interval. The hypothesis on eventual slopes supplies the required frequent slope estimates for the negative profile. Letting $\varepsilon$ decrease to zero gives $r(t)\ge-6/(1+4t)$, including the right endpoint.

For the first interval, $t_0=0$ and $r_0(0)\ge-6$ supply the initial comparison. Suppose the bound holds on interval $i$. At its right endpoint, the jump condition gives
$$r_{i+1}(t_{i+1})\ge r_i(t_{i+1})\ge-\frac6{1+4t_{i+1}}.$$
This starts the same comparison on interval $i+1$. Induction proves the claim on every interval. In particular, both one-sided profile values at each joining time satisfy the bound.

The analytic comparison is the step used in [Kleiner-Lott, proof of Lemma 79.11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=154), with the scalar differential inequality from Appendix B. Its geometric application requires separately verifying the profile hypotheses for a Ricci flow.

theorem.theorem_title: Scalar lower bound across upward jumps
theorem.formal_statement:
theorem OpenGA.scalar_lower_bound_across_upward_jumps
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (times : ℕ → ℝ) (profiles : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hzero : times 0 = 0)
    (htimes : ∀ i < n, times i < times (i + 1))
    (hcont : ∀ i < n, ContinuousOn (profiles i) (Icc (times i) (times (i + 1))))
    (hinitial : -6 ≤ profiles 0 (times 0))
    (hslope : ∀ i < n, ∀ t ∈ Ico (times i) (times (i + 1)), ∀ q : ℝ,
      q < (2 / 3 : ℝ) * (profiles i t) ^ 2 →
        ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] t, q < slope (profiles i) t s)
    (hjumps : ∀ i, i + 1 < n →
      profiles i (times (i + 1)) ≤ profiles (i + 1) (times (i + 1))) :
    ∀ i < n, ∀ t ∈ Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)),
      -(6 : ℝ) / (1 + 4 * t) ≤ profiles i t := by sorry
theorem.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n$. For $0\le i<n$, let $r_i:[t_i,t_{i+1}]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Write
$$D_+r_i(t)=\liminf_{s\to t^+}\frac{r_i(s)-r_i(t)}{s-t}.$$
Assume $r_0(0)\ge-6$, and, for each $i<n$ and $t_i\le t<t_{i+1}$,
$$D_+r_i(t)\ge\frac23r_i(t)^2.$$
At every internal joining time, assume $r_i(t_{i+1})\le r_{i+1}(t_{i+1})$ for $i+1<n$. Then
$$r_i(t)\ge-\frac6{1+4t}\qquad(0\le i<n,\ t_i\le t\le t_{i+1}).$$
This isolates the scalar comparison step used in Kleiner-Lott's surgery estimates, with upward jumps allowed. Applying it to scalar-curvature minima requires establishing these analytic hypotheses from the geometry; this statement does not itself formalize a Ricci flow.

[Source: Kleiner-Lott, proof of Lemma 79.11, p. 154](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=154), using [Appendix B, equations (B.1)-(B.2), p. 202](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0605667v5#page=202).
